3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner in substance is that the suit land originally belonged to Md Taslimuddin Sarker and Md Mohsinuddin Sarker against whom there was a rent decree in Rent Suit No. 889 of 1942. Md Mahbub Hossain Prodhan purchased the suit land along with other land in auction on 11-12-1942 in Rent Execution Case No. 1955 of 1942 and accordingly, got delivery of possession through Court on 5-5-1943. Said Mahbub Hossain being the owner inpossession granted settlement of the suit land for agriculture purpose in favour of the plaintiff school on 2nd Baishakh, 1352 BS on receipt of salami of Taka 500.00. The secretary of the plaintiff-school late Delwar Hossain Chowdhury took possession of the land on behalf of the school. The plaintiff-school has been possessing the suit land through cultivation bargadar. The responsibility of getting the SA Khatian recorded in the name of the school was with late Delwar Hossain Chowdhury being secretary in respect of the suit land as all documents of the school were, in his custody. He was killed on 30-11-1971 during liberation war. On 24-7-74, Tahsilder refused to accept rent from the school on the plea that the suit lands were recorded with other land in SA Khatian No. 33 in the name of Kasiruddin Chowdhury and Karimuddin Chowdhury. The plaintiff further stated that the aforesaid persons had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land as those persons died long before SA Khatian. In spite of wrong preparation of SA Khatian the school is still in possession of the suit land and that the school authority submitted Return to the Government in respect of the suit land under President's Order No. 98 of 1972. 

 10. Mr Md Nazibar Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that' the learned District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not properly adverting to the trial Court's finding regarding prima facie and arguable case of the plaintiffs and balance of convenience and inconvenience of the parties. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff-school submitted a large number of documents such as sale certificate; copy of the writ of delivery of possession, several receipts of payment of rents and the Return under President's Order 98 of 1972 as to the ownership of the suit land and further submits that Kasimuddin Chowdhury and Kisimuddin Chowdhury died in 1922 and 1938 respectively long before the enactment of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. But the learned District Judge did not consider those documents in its true perspective and committed error of law which resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice.
